one_line: Start with free public evidence, verify the artifact type and retain the result. A paid request is optional. The six-step worked example below covers request-attestation only, not every product.
amounts: No amount is written here. The only authority on an amount is accepts[] in the 402 you receive. Amounts are set per request in the payment challenge and can change; your wallet signs exactly the amount shown and nothing more.
self_payments: Payments from the operator's own wallets are recorded as self-tests and never counted as buyers or revenue. Authoritative flag: settled_usdc.excludes_self=true on /api/revenue.

steps.name: discover
steps.expect: 200 JSON: x402Version, scheme, network, asset, payTo, resources[] of {method, url}. Discovery and verification are free; stop after a useful free result unless a paid output is explicitly wanted.

steps.name: request
steps.expect: 402 JSON; csoai.preview lists the signed cards already on file for the subject, free. Retain the selected artifact and its source date; a preview is not a new measurement or a purchase.

HTTP 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header and a JSON body: x402Version, accepts[] of {scheme, network, asset, payTo, amount, maxAmountRequired, maxTimeoutSeconds}, extensions.offer-receipt.info.offers[] (JWS, verifiable offline)

steps.name: settle
steps.who_pays: the caller, from the caller's own wallet; this site holds no key for you and never settles on your behalf
steps.expect: Only after an explicit paid request and approval of the current accepts[] entry: the client signs an authorisation for that entry and retries the same URL with the payment header. These instructions do not themselves authorise payment.

steps.name: receive
steps.expect: 200 JSON {card, verify, signed, unsigned_reason, bytes, note}; card is a card-v0 with surface ras.commission and payload.settle {network, transaction, payer}; header x-payment-response carries the settlement response, with a signed receipt when the facilitator names a payer and the signing key is present. Scope: request-attestation records only; /api/commissions is not an all-product delivery ledger. Retain the actual response bytes and follow the purchased product's retrieval instructions. An empty or unreadable lookup does not prove failed delivery. Do not make another payment solely because a lookup is empty. RETRIEVABLE and CARDS_PUBLISHED are retrieval states, not buyer acceptance.

steps.name: verify
also: https://councilof.ai/verifier/gspc-verify.mjs for the measurement cards the receipt references
https://councilof.ai/verifier/verify_receipt.py for the signed offer and receipt
steps.expect: VALID (exit 0), INVALID (exit 1) or UNCHECKABLE (exit 2). Use the checker for the received artifact format, not one checker for every product. Verify Merkle inclusion only when a proof is supplied. Signature validity is not measurement truth, payment verification or buyer acceptance.

offer_receipt_checker.format: x402 compact JWS offer/receipt, not card-v0
offer_receipt_checker.default_network: One public DID-document read; saved DID file supports offline replay

assembled_feed_checker.scope: Assembled payload.blocks and optional unsigned response/request records; not signature or payment verification
